prompt: Recover abandoned cart sales by sending timely, personalized email reminders to customers before they lose interest.

intent.desiredOutcome: Recover abandoned cart sales by sending timely, personalized email reminders to customers before they lose interest.
intent.cronHint: every 30 minutes (to catch carts at the configured abandonment threshold)
intent.qualityBrief: A solid version handles: (1) Configurable abandonment delay (e.g., 1–24 hours) set by the merchant, (2) One email per abandoned cart (idempotency — never send duplicates), (3) Respects customer email preferences and opt-outs, (4) Excludes carts already converted to orders, (5) Admin panel showing recent reminders sent and open rate tracking (optional but valuable). Common pitfall: sending multiple reminders to the same cart; track 'reminded_at' to prevent this.

edgeCases: Cart already converted to an order before the cron fires — exclude by checking Shopify's abandonedCheckouts for carts that have a completed_at timestamp
Customer has unsubscribed from marketing emails or has no email address — check email marketing consent before sending and skip silently
Cron fires twice within the same window due to scheduler overlap — use FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED on the DB queue and check reminded_at IS NULL before processing
Same cart updated (items added/removed) after the abandonment threshold — use the cart's updated_at to reset the abandonment clock so reminders reflect the latest cart contents
Customer is a guest with no Shopify customer record — guest checkouts have no customer_id; handle null customer_id and use the email captured at checkout directly
Merchant changes the abandonment delay while a batch is in-flight — evaluate delay against the settings row at cron start, not per-item, so the batch is internally consistent

uxExpectations.admin: Dashboard should lead with a summary of recovery performance (emails sent, estimated recovered revenue) followed by a paginated log of recent reminders with cart value, customer identity, sent timestamp, and status. Settings panel for abandonment delay should be prominent and immediately actionable.

platformGaps.gap: Shopify does not expose a native abandoned checkout webhook that fires at a merchant-configurable delay
platformGaps.mitigation: Cron job polls abandonedCheckouts via Admin GraphQL every 30 minutes, computes elapsed time since updatedAt against the merchant-configured delay stored in the settings table, and filters candidates in-app

platformGaps.gap: No batch write API for sending emails — each cart reminder requires an individual platform.email.send call
platformGaps.mitigation: Pre-fetch all abandoned checkout and customer data in bulk before the loop via shopify.graphqlPaginate; per-item email.send calls inside the loop are unavoidable for this resource type

platformGaps.gap: Open rate tracking requires a pixel or click-back signal that the platform email service does not expose
platformGaps.mitigation: Track delivery status only (sent/failed) in the reminders table; surface sent count and estimated recovery (orders placed within 24h of reminder) as a proxy metric via the Admin GraphQL orders query

emailSpec.purpose: Fires once per abandoned cart when the cart has been idle longer than the merchant-configured abandonment delay and the customer has not yet completed checkout

cronBatching.description: Before the loop begins, bulk-fetch all abandoned checkouts updated more than (abandonment_delay_hours) ago and not yet completed via graphqlPaginate on abandonedCheckouts. In the same pre-fetch pass, collect the customer IDs from those checkouts and resolve customer email marketing consent status via batched customer lookups. Filter out any checkout tokens already present in cart_reminders with a non-null reminded_at. The loop then operates only on pre-resolved data with no per-item Shopify read calls.

cronContract.handlerMustProduce: For each candidate abandoned checkout, the handler must resolve before acting: (1) checkout_token as the idempotency key, (2) customer display name (first + last name or email prefix) for email personalization, (3) customer_email — either from the Shopify customer record or the guest email captured on the checkout, (4) customer email marketing consent status — skip and record as 'skipped' if the customer has opted out or consent is unknown, (5) cart_total_amount and cart_currency for the email subject line and body, (6) cart_line_items_json — a serialized array of { title, quantity, price, image_url } for the product list in the email body, (7) checkout_url — the Shopify recovery URL the CTA button points to, (8) cart_abandoned_at — the checkout's updatedAt timestamp used to confirm the abandonment window has elapsed. The handler must verify no row exists in cart_reminders for checkout_token with reminded_at IS NOT NULL before proceeding to send. After a successful send, it must upsert cart_reminders setting status='sent' and reminded_at=now(). On email send failure it must upsert with status='failed' and failure_reason set to the error message.
